Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and learned AGA for the State.

2. This application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. has been preferred for quashing of the entire proceedings,
including summoning order dated 26.06.2023, of complaint case No. 6055 of 2021 (Pragya Patel Vs.
Anubhav Gangwar and others), under Section 306 IPC, P.S. Ait, District Jalaun, pending in the court of C.J.M., Jalaun at Orai, on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties.

sentences.text: It has been submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that essentially the matter relates to matrimonial dispute.
The daughter of deceased was married with applicant no.1.
The deceased has suffered natural death.

The first information report was lodged by the opposite party no.2 on 07.01.2021 under Section 306 IPC but after investigation, it was found that deceased has not committed suicide and charge-sheet was submitted only for offence under Sections 498A, 506 I.P.C.
and Section 3/4 D.P. Act.
After that the opposite party no.2 has lodged the impugned complaint under Section 306 IPC.
Now both the parties have amicably settled the dispute and compromised the matter.
In accordance with compromise, other cases have already been quashed.
It was submitted that in the instant matter, there is no material to attract Section 306 IPC and thus, the impugned proceedings may be quashed on the basis of compromise between the parties.

In this connection, learned counsel has referred case of Iqbal Singh Sandhu and others Vs. State of Punjab and others 2024 LawSuit (P&H) 772.
4.

entities.text: Iqbal Singh Sandhu and others Vs. State of Punjab and others 2024 LawSuit (P&H) 772
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 has concurred with the arguments of learned counsel for the applicants and submitted that both the parties have amicably settled the dispute and compromised the matter and thus, the impugned proceedings may be quashed on the basis of compromise.
5. Learned A.G.A. has no objection if parties compromise the matter.
6. I have considered the submissions and perused the record.
7. It is well settled that in appropriate cases criminal proceedings may be quashed on the basis of compromise.

Generally, the proceedings for offences under Section 306 IPC can not be quashed on the basis of compromise between the parties but in the instant matter, it would be pertinent to mention that during investigation, no case under Section 306 IPC was found and after that the impugned complaint was filed.

The impugned complaint was lodged by the wife of applicant no.1,
alleging that applicants have made demand of dowry and on that account they have subjected her father to mental cruelty and that on 28.09.2020 while father of complainant has gone to the house of applicants-accused, they have insulted and threatened him to send to jail in false case and due to these reasons, the father of complainant was disturbed.
It was further alleged by the complainant that due to depression, on 21.12.2020 her father committed suicide but her post-mortem was not conducted.
Applicant no.1 is son-in-law of deceased and remaining applicants are father, mother and brother of applicant no.1.
The post-mortem of deceased has not been conducted and there is no such medical evidence that deceased has committed suicide.

Neither there is medical evidence that deceased has committed suicide nor there is such credible evidence that applicants have abetted the deceased to commit suicide and in fact there is no credible evidence to attract Section 306 IPC.

Essentially the case is outcome of matrimonial dispute and thus the dispute between the parties appears to be private in nature and if parties compromise the matter, it would not have adverse impact on society.

Both the parties have amicably settled all dispute and agreed for quashing of impugned proceedings vide settlement deed dated 02.08.2024, arrived before Mediation &
Conciliation Centre of this Court, the copy of which is available on record.
In view of these facts and circumstances, no useful purpose would be served by exhausting the remedy of trial and it would be in the interest of justice that impugned proceedings be quashed.
